item.title: Fixing 'conda: command not found' After Anaconda Installation
item.description:
“Fixing ‘conda: command not found’ After Anaconda Installation”

When setting up a new environment with Anaconda or Miniconda, receiving the error -bash: conda: command not found (or similar on other shells) indicates that the installation directory for the conda executable is not correctly included in your system’s PATH environment variable. This prevents the shell from locating and executing the command.

How can one reliably configure the system’s PATH to make conda accessible from the terminal across various operating systems and shell configurations?

item.title: macOS Environment Variables: Global Settings for Apps & Terminal
item.description:
“macOS Environment Variables: Global Settings for Apps & Terminal”

Setting environment variables in macOS to be accessible by all applications, including those launched via Spotlight, requires careful configuration. Unlike some other operating systems, macOS has specific mechanisms for managing these settings. The primary challenge is ensuring that both command-line interfaces (like Terminal) and graphical user interface (GUI) applications can access the same variables.

Several methods have been proposed and used over the years, with varying degrees of success and compatibility across different macOS versions. The most effective approaches often involve system-level configurations or custom launch agents.
